From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary point:** The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" says the [STANDARD] clauses are cleared by both sides and need no scrutiny. That is not our position. Nothing here has been agreed by Wattlebridge, and the note comes from the Seller's draft, not from our instructions. I reviewed every item against the playbook, and the [STANDARD] items below are mostly well outside it.

**Fallback authority:** Amelia Frost has given no written authority for the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Neither can be offered or implied until she does.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6.0M.** The Seller's figure is our fallback, which we cannot use without Frost's written authority identifying this draft, and none exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation: Reject all three elements.** Each threshold is 5x our position and the deductible structure removes recovery of the first AUD 250k.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a statement that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general claims, with the time limit confined to general claims.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval (none given), and the "applies to all Claims" wording would pull fundamental and fraud claims under the short limit.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties get the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Title and capacity go to the core of what we are buying, and "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap them at AUD 4.8M for 18 months.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: Insert the carve-out expressly and reject the "any nature" wording.** This protection cannot be waived or traded, and as drafted the Seller could contractually shield its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Deemed disclosure of the entire data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only.
- **Recommendation: Reject the general disclosures and limit disclosure to specific items.** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would let the Seller disclose away most warranties. Para 1.4 (non-admission) should also be checked so it cannot be read as limiting Buyer remedies.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion deleted.
- **Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3.** If a qualifier is ever conceded, it should be Seller knowledge only, with named knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and it must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject and make both a hard condition precedent.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6M), and the Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits there is no consent and no evidence of conditions being met. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-completion release.** The facility (about AUD 3.2M) is unrepaid with no discharge (Disclosure Letter para 3). A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking plus Frost's approval, and neither exists.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer should want:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) shown as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation: Reject silent exclusion and require an express mechanism.** "A matter for the Seller" is not a binding allocation, and the Disclosure Letter (para 5) does not say whether on-costs apply, so we should request that detail.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A broader IP indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure (payment of every SOW3 fee triggers transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3).
- **Recommendation: Broaden the indemnity and keep the SOW3 cure.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way (DD-010 is not bank verification), so we should not treat it as owed or as paid. We should request payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer should want:** Log preservation, investigation, and regular updates, with no assumptions about the outcome.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not assert a breach either.** The facts are unresolved (about 1,240 records, access unknown, notification unknown). We should require preservation, investigation, cooperation and updates, with no numeric demand in either direction.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** An assessment of the renewals, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: Neither accept the Seller's label nor claim a deduction yet.** Request the contracts and confirm termination rights, accrual and timing, since the Disclosure Letter (para 8) does not say whether they are unavoidable or ordinary course.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply uniformly to all Claims, with tax/IP settled "under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: Reject the uniform application.** Each category needs its own regime, and a catch-all would silently override the specific protections.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register (DD-012).
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation: Do not treat DD-012 as proof.** It is a company-supplied internal source, and the Disclosure Letter (para 10) concedes that Buyer verification is not complete. Require independent evidence (for example share transfer history, third-party searches for encumbrances, and authority approvals), backed by the fundamental regime.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms kept open and negotiated separately.
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled" and record both as OPEN.** Equally, we should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution in our own mark-up.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Prepare the mark-up on the playbook starting positions, with no fallbacks offered.
2. Send the Seller a document request list covering Bluefen consent conditions, the Riverlark payout and release, Ironquay payment evidence, bonus on-costs, Sandbar contracts, DD-006 logs and the independent title evidence.
3. If the team wants room to move on the cap or time limit, ask Amelia Frost for written authority identifying the specific draft.
